query: What drives customer satisfaction (Overall Rating) across the different airlines?

per_column.name: Service_Score_Mean
per_column.rationale: Mean of the service sub-dimension ratings (Seat Comfort, Staff Service, Food & Beverages, Inflight Entertainment, Value For Money). Values top out at 5, consistent with a 1-5 average, and it is distinct from the Overall Rating scale. It plausibly carries strong signal about satisfaction and is not a function of overall_rating. Caveat: it is only an aggregate of columns already present, so its NEW leverage beyond the original sub-ratings is limited, but it is a legitimate predictor.

per_column.name: Weakest_Service_Dim
per_column.rationale: Categorical label of which service dimension scored lowest. Derived from the sub-rating columns, external to overall_rating, and plausibly predictive (which aspect fails can shape overall satisfaction). Legitimate predictor, though again a transformation of existing sub-ratings.

per_column.name: Value_Gap
per_column.rationale: A signed difference (0.25-step values from ~-2.75 to 2) between value-for-money and the service mean. It is a mismatch/interaction feature built from sub-ratings, not from overall_rating, and can carry predictive signal. Legitimate predictor.

per_column.name: Airline_Avg_Rating
per_column.rationale: This is the group mean of the FOCUS variable (average Overall Rating per airline). It is computed directly from overall_rating values and includes the target aggregated over the airline. As full-sample target encoding of an existing column, it leaks the outcome (rows share their own target's group mean) and is only knowable from the labels. Not a clean predictor.

per_column.name: Rating_vs_Airline_Avg
per_column.rationale: This is overall_rating minus the airline average, i.e. a deterministic residual of the focus variable. overall_rating can be exactly recovered as Rating_vs_Airline_Avg + Airline_Avg_Rating. It restates/leaks the target and must be excluded.

per_column.name: Is_Premium_Class
per_column.rationale: Binary flag derived from the Class column indicating premium travel. External to overall_rating and plausibly predictive of satisfaction. Legitimate predictor (a re-encoding of an existing categorical).

per_column.name: Satisfaction_Tier
per_column.rationale: A high/mid/low tier of 'satisfaction', which is the focus concept itself; this is almost certainly a discretization/binning of the Overall Rating (or an equivalent satisfaction measure). It restates the target and cannot serve as an independent predictor without leaking.

per_column.name: Service_Score_Std
per_column.rationale: Standard deviation across the service sub-dimension ratings, capturing consistency/dispersion of the experience. Derived from sub-ratings, external to overall_rating, and can carry incremental (nonlinear/interaction) signal. Legitimate predictor.

judge.rationale: Five of eight columns are legitimate predictors (Service_Score_Mean, Weakest_Service_Dim, Value_Gap, Is_Premium_Class, Service_Score_Std), but each is essentially an aggregation or re-encoding of columns already in the original table (the five service sub-ratings and Class). They add convenient summaries, dispersion, and interaction terms, but only modest NEW predictive leverage beyond the raw sub-ratings a model already sees. Three columns are disqualified: Airline_Avg_Rating (target-encoded group mean of overall_rating) and Rating_vs_Airline_Avg (deterministic residual of overall_rating) are outcome leakage, and Satisfaction_Tier is a restatement/binning of the focus. The set's genuine incremental predictive value is therefore limited, hence a low-moderate score.
